Striatal destruction is the lesion behind the extrapyramidal movement disorder, which is the clinical feature the disease is named for in the 2019 series.
Basal ganglia degeneration and the neurological regression are reported as one clinical picture in this disease, the regression being what the striatal damage costs the child.

Severe dysarthria accompanies the movement disorder in the families in which it was described. The causal direction here is the curator's inference, not the source's claim: the source says "often accompanied by", which is co-occurrence. Dystonic dysarthria from orofacial and laryngeal involvement is the clinically expected reading in a generalised dystonia, but these patients also have the language loss of the developmental regression, and no source separates the two contributions.

edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are not neurons, and the affected structures - striatum, brainstem - have never been studied directly in this disease. The rescue establishes causality and says nothing about tissue selectivity. The fibroblast assay also under-reads the defect: the reviewed series found residual activity up to 86 percent of control in fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Two damaged copies of NDUFAF6 (formerly C8orf38), which encodes a mitochondrial complex I assembly factor. The reported spectrum spans several mutation classes. Across the 24 patients tallied in the 2026 review, eighteen distinct variants have been reported - ten missense, one nonsense, two splice-site, four frameshift and two small in-frame duplications - and roughly half of those patients carry a single recurrent missense allele, c.371T>C p.Ile124Thr. The largest single cohort adds nineteen further distinct variants from eighteen families. Only the canonical transcript NM_152416.4 encodes the mitochondrially targeted protein, which is why a deep intronic variant altering isoform choice can be pathogenic without changing any coding sequence.

nodes.description:
Symmetrical destruction of the striatum, putamen first. In the deeply phenotyped kindred the lesions were cytotoxic, involved proliferation of the lenticulo-striate arteries, and spread from putamen to caudate before cavitating with volume loss. Across the published literature the putamen was involved in every case in which the basal ganglia were described, and the caudate in fewer than half. This tissue selectivity - rather than the enzyme deficiency, which is present in fibroblasts and muscle too - is what makes the disease a neurological one.
The cell type bound below is inferred rather than sourced. No NDUFAF6 study names a cell type: the imaging and the one published description of the lesion are at tissue level, and no neuropathology has been reported for any patient. Medium spiny neurons are the principal projection neuron of the striatum and so are the cell the lesion is presumed to destroy, but which striatal populations are lost, and in what order, is unknown in this disease.

nodes.description: NDUFS8 is a core subunit of the Q module. Without NDUFAF6 it is not incorporated, and the module does not mature. The consequence is visible on patient gels as a module-graded loss of subunits: Q-module NDUFS3 falls dramatically, N-module NDUFS1 intermediately, and P-module NDUFB11 least. That gradient is itself informative, because it is the known turnover order of complex I modules when assembly fails rather than a random loss.

nodes.description: Concurrent infection is the named precipitant of the metabolic crises that punctuate this disease's course, and avoiding metabolic stressors of this kind is an explicit management aim. The mechanism is not measured in any NDUFAF6 study; the general account is that the increased energy demand of febrile illness is not met by a cell already running on reduced complex I, so the exposure is recorded as exacerbating the existing bioenergetic deficit rather than as initiating anything.

nodes.description: Too little functioning NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase, with the other respiratory chain complexes spared. The deficiency is partial rather than complete and the residual activity has been quantified: across the reviewed cases, residual respiratory chain complex activity was 40 to 86 percent of control in cultured fibroblasts and 28 to 80 percent in muscle. That residual enzyme is the most likely explanation for the comparatively preserved motor function this disease shows against other Leigh syndrome genotypes, and it is also why a near-normal fibroblast assay does not exclude the diagnosis.

nodes.description: NDUFAF6 acts at the initial stages of complex I assembly. It is a mitochondria-targeted 333-amino-acid peripheral membrane protein of the squalene and phytoene synthase family, an assignment that is itself informative: sequence and structure suggest it retains some enzymatic activity, but one that has diverged considerably from the canonical members of that family, so what it actually catalyses here is not established. Not every metazoan has an ortholog, which means complex I biogenesis does not require it in all organisms. Losing it removes a component from the step at which the nuclear-encoded matrix arm and the mtDNA-encoded membrane arm are first brought together.

nodes.description: Intermittent episodes of metabolic decompensation precipitated by concurrent infection. These are the acute events that punctuate an otherwise gradual course, and in the largest cohort they are where the stepwise losses happen: one sibling recovered completely from an early decompensation while another died of one. Avoiding metabolic stressors is consequently a management aim rather than only a prognostic observation.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from patients, complemented with the wild-type gene. This is the experiment that made NDUFAF6 a disease gene and it has been repeated independently across the reports: in the 2011 C8orf38 characterisation, in the 2016 Leigh gene identification, and in the 2019 three-sibling kindred.

Loss of the assembled CI/III2/IV supercomplex, with homodimeric complex III accumulating in its place. This is a recognised downstream signature of complex I assembly defects rather than a separate lesion, and it is recorded here because it is measured directly in this disease's patient material.
